title.en: Watch a TLS handshake and its version
title.hinglish: TLS handshake aur uska version dekho

why.en: Connects to example.com and prints the negotiated TLS version, cipher and certificate details, the result of the Client Hello and Server Hello steps.
why.hinglish: example.com se connect karke negotiated TLS version, cipher aur certificate details print karta hai, jo Client Hello aur Server Hello steps ka result hai.

expect.en: Lines like 'TLSv1.3', 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384' or 'TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256', and the certificate subject and issuer. The curl -v output shows the same handshake as '* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello'. Exact cipher and issuer vary.
expect.hinglish: 'TLSv1.3', 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384' ya 'TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256' jaisi lines, aur certificate subject aur issuer. curl -v output wahi handshake '* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello' ki tarah dikhata hai. Exact cipher aur issuer badalte hain.

why.en: The browser checks Not Before and Not After. This prints them for example.com so you can see how an expired certificate would be caught.
why.hinglish: Browser Not Before aur Not After check karta hai. Ye example.com ke liye unhe print karta hai taaki dikhe expired certificate kaise pakda jaata hai.

commands.unix: openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com < /dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates -subject -issuer
commands.windows: $tcp = New-Object Net.Sockets.TcpClient('example.com',443); $ssl = New-Object Net.Security.SslStream($tcp.GetStream()); $ssl.AuthenticateAsClient('example.com'); $ssl.RemoteCertificate | Select Subject, Issuer, NotBefore, NotAfter

expect.en: notBefore and notAfter dates (or NotBefore/NotAfter in PowerShell), plus subject and issuer. The dates differ over time as the certificate is renewed.
expect.hinglish: notBefore aur notAfter dates (PowerShell mein NotBefore/NotAfter), saath mein subject aur issuer. Certificate renew hone par dates badalti rehti hain.

title.en: Find the Client Hello and its SNI
title.hinglish: Client Hello aur uska SNI dhoondo

why.en: Open the lesson's .pcap in Wireshark. The Client Hello is sent in clear text, so the site name in server_name is visible.
why.hinglish: Lesson ka .pcap Wireshark mein kholo. Client Hello clear text mein jaata hai, isliye server_name mein site ka naam dikhta hai.

expect.en: A Client Hello packet. Expand it to see supported_versions, key_share and server_name (example.com).
expect.hinglish: Ek Client Hello packet. Ise expand karo to supported_versions, key_share aur server_name (example.com) dikhenge.

title.en: See what is encrypted after Server Hello
title.hinglish: Server Hello ke baad kya encrypted hai dekho

why.en: In TLS 1.3 the certificate is encrypted, so it appears as Application Data. Compare with the TLS 1.2 scenario where it is readable.
why.hinglish: TLS 1.3 mein certificate encrypted hai, isliye Application Data ki tarah dikhta hai. TLS 1.2 scenario se compare karo jahan wo padha ja sakta hai.

expect.en: In the TLS 1.3 capture there is no readable Certificate message, only Application Data records. In the TLS 1.2 capture a Certificate message is shown.
expect.hinglish: TLS 1.3 capture mein padhne layak Certificate message nahi hota, sirf Application Data records. TLS 1.2 capture mein Certificate message dikhta hai.
